mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has printed below -30 in all four visible weeks, and transit station footfall is the tightest co-mover with discretionary retail trips. With no easing signal in any observable series, the same transit suppression persists, so the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC prints below the last 28-day mean of -29.0.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds -29.0 while TRANSIT stays below -30 in at least three of the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM jumped 6.1 points to 0.0 in the latest week, the pre-restriction stock-up signature. Households that front-load essential purchases cut discretionary shopping in the following weeks, dragging RETAIL_REC down over a two-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by 5 points or more week-on-week, or crosses above its own four-week mean
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved -6.1 at t-1w to 0.0 at t-0w, a +6.1 point jump
regime_hint: escalating case growth ahead of restrictions
failure_condition: The two-week mean of RETAIL_REC after a 5-point-or-larger GROCERY_PHARM jump is equal to or above the two-week mean before the jump.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES rebounded 15.4 points in t-0w while TRANSIT rebounded only 7.3 points, showing office commuting returning faster than leisure and transit-dependent travel. The gap leaves discretionary retail trips suppressed and RETAIL_REC below its trailing mean over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES recovers 10 points or more week-on-week while TRANSIT recovers less than half that amount
evidence_refs: fact:t-1w to t-0w: WORKPLACES -37.3 to -21.9 (+15.4) vs TRANSIT -38.9 to -31.6 (+7.3)
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES rebounds 10 points or more with TRANSIT lagging by half or more, the following two-week RETAIL_REC mean is at or above the preceding two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restriction regime, signalled by RESIDENTIAL above +12.0 alongside WORKPLACES below -35 (both observed in t-1w), authorities cap capacity and shorten hours at discretionary venues. That clampdown propagates to retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above +12.0 and WORKPLACES below -35.0 in the same week
failure_condition: In weeks where RESIDENTIAL exceeds +12 and WORKPLACES falls below -35, the subsequent 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not below the preceding 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: December is Tokyo's peak retail month, driven by year-end bonuses, gift buying and New Year sales, and the PARKS series shows an ordinary winter seasonal decline rather than a new clampdown. Holiday spending lifts RETAIL_REC above the -29.0 trailing mean over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -10.4 at t-3w to -20.9 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC improved from -31.6 to -27.9
regime_hint: holiday shopping season without new formal restrictions
failure_condition: The RETAIL_REC mean from 2020-12-15 to 2021-01-12 is at or below -29.0 while no visible mobility series tightens below its four-week minimum.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has stayed at or above +9.4 in all four visible weeks, showing a durable home-centric routine. As long as the residential series does not fall back toward baseline, out-of-home discretionary trips stay suppressed and RETAIL_REC stays below its trailing mean over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below +5.0 for two consecutive weeks while RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks remains below its prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of elevated RESIDENTIAL (stay-at-home intensity) with GROCERY_PHARM at 0.0 (essential spend fully normalised) marks a wallet reallocation toward essentials. Discretionary categories lose share within the same week, so RETAIL_REC falls over the following seven days.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM at or above 0.0 while RESIDENTIAL is at or above +9.0 in the same week
failure_condition: In weeks with GROCERY_PHARM at or above 0.0 and RESIDENTIAL at or above +9.0, RETAIL_REC rises over the following 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: The t-0w rebound in TRANSIT (-38.9 to -31.6) and WORKPLACES (-37.3 to -21.9) shows mobility resilience after the t-1w dip. When week-on-week transit improvement reaches 5 points, discretionary retail footfall follows with roughly a two-week lag, lifting RETAIL_REC above its trailing mean.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by 5 points or more week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:t-1w to t-0w TRANSIT -38.9 to -31.6 (+7.3) and WORKPLACES -37.3 to -21.9 (+15.4)
failure_condition: In weeks where TRANSIT improves by 5 points or more, the following two-week RETAIL_REC mean is not above the preceding two-week mean.
